criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (reef bleaching monitoring with fluid lensing), rationale and single-spacecraft choice are clearly argued and cited. Users are vague: customers are named but the operator is not identified beyond 'Australia ground facilities'. Wikipedia is cited as a source, and several claims lack support.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.
Thus, only one satellite is required.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Good coverage of all space-segment items with STK access data, ground tracks and a Keplerian element table. However, the launch choice is contradictory (piggyback versus direct launch, unbuilt Vega E). RAAN is wrongly tied to the launch site. The altitude logic is inconsistent, no swath or delta-v calculations are shown, and the EOL strategy is unresolved. Access table has a duplicated row. Citations to tables are not in the bibliography.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion recaps the segments and notes launch-vehicle risk with a fallback option, which is a reasonable conclusion. It is largely a restatement, however, and does not weigh the unresolved issues (EOL compliance, altitude trade-off, launch contradictions) against the evidence.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear section structure, contents list and headings. Writing has several grammar and typo errors ('a Earth', 'purposed', 'complied'). Figures and tables lack numbers and titles, and in-text citations such as [49]-[74] do not match the 10-item bibliography. Stray characters appear in references.

technical_issues.issue: Piggyback rideshare is described, yet the Executive Summary says 'direct launch' and the Orbit section says the satellite 'can be launched directly'. Vega E is unbuilt, with a first flight of 2024 that is unsupported.
RAAN 27.33° is stated to indicate the launch facility location. Kourou is near 53°W, so this is incorrect, and the epoch is not given.
Altitude reasoning contradicts itself: resolution must be high enough, yet high altitude 'yields low resolution images which is also desirable'. No swath width or GSD calculation is shown.
Perturbation and delta-v calculations are claimed in the Executive Summary but not shown. Orbit insertion manoeuvre is omitted.
Tasmania (~42°S) is described as a near-pole facility choice. Access table lists a duplicate row 15 identical to row 14, and a stray '----' row.
Claim that the descending side is 'constantly in sunlight' is wrong. Eclipse depends on beta angle, and local time of the node is not stated.

Passive uncontrolled decay from 600 km takes decades to centuries, failing the 25-year guideline. The text says the drag sail is the 'most promising alternative' but leaves the EOL decision unresolved and contains a truncated sentence.
Tables cite [49]-[74] and Falcon table cites [10], none of which match the 10-entry bibliography. [10] is also used for the drag-sail source. Wikipedia [6] is used, which is not accepted.

overall: Solid, mostly complete space-segment design with STK evidence, but significant technical contradictions (launch vehicle, RAAN, altitude trade-off, EOL compliance) and unsupported claims. Figures and tables are unlabelled and citations are inconsistent, with Wikipedia used. Weighted score approximately 49/100.

feedback.summary: You have built a clear, mostly complete space-segment design for reef bleaching monitoring, supported by STK access data, ground tracks and a Keplerian element table. The main weaknesses are internal contradictions and unsupported claims: the launch vehicle, RAAN, altitude trade-off and end-of-life plan need to be made consistent and backed by calculations. Figure, table and citation fixes would also lift the presentation.
next_steps: Resolve the launch contradiction first: choose one operational vehicle, justify it, and remove the 'direct launch' wording that conflicts with your piggyback rideshare description.
Add the missing calculations: orbit insertion and delta-v, perturbation effects, and the altitude trade-off with swath width and GSD. Correct the RAAN explanation and state the epoch.

Fix the ground and end-of-life content: justify your ground station choice (Tasmania is not near-pole), replace the sunlight claim with beta angle and local time, remove the duplicate access row, and commit to a disposal method that meets the 25-year guideline.

criteria.C1: Your mission purpose (reef bleaching monitoring with fluid lensing) and single-spacecraft rationale are clearly argued. To reach the next level, name the operator explicitly rather than only 'Australia ground facilities', and state who operates the spacecraft and who uses its data. Replace the Wikipedia source with peer-reviewed or agency literature, and support key claims with references that appear in your bibliography.
criteria.C2: Your space-segment coverage is strong, including STK access data, ground tracks and a Keplerian element table. To reach the next level, use one verified, operational launch vehicle throughout and correct the RAAN explanation, which does not indicate the launch site; state the epoch too. Show calculations for resolution, swath, GSD and delta-v, including orbit insertion. Settle a compliant end-of-life plan, since passive decay from 600 km fails the 25-year guideline.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion recaps the mission segments and sensibly flags launch-vehicle risk with a fallback option, which is a good start. To reach the next level, draw conclusions from your evidence, such as whether the chosen orbit meets your resolution and sun-illumination goals, and whether your end-of-life plan is compliant. Weigh the unresolved contradictions rather than restating the design, and state clearly what the evidence does and does not yet show.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear structure, a contents list and an executive summary that covers the key points. To reach the next level, proofread for spelling and grammar, including errors such as 'a Earth', 'purposed' and 'complied'. Number and title every figure and table, and use a consistent format. Make in-text citations match the bibliography: the table citations [49]-[74] and the reused [10] must be corrected, and the Wikipedia reference replaced.
